transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: No, I don’t, Bernard.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I think you know that I’ve opposed the death penalty during all of my life.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I don’t see any evidence that it’s a deterrent, and I think there are better and more effective ways to deal with violent crime.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve done so in my own state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And it’s one of the reasons why we have had the biggest drop in crime of any industrial state in America; why we have the lowest murder rate of any industrial state in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But we have work to do in this nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We have work to do to fight a real war, not a phony war, against drugs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And that’s something I want to lead, something we haven’t had over the course of the past many years, even though the Vice President has been at least allegedly in charge of that war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We have much to do to step up that war, to double the number of drug enforcement agents, to fight both here and abroad, to work with our neighbors in this hemisphere.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I want to call a hemispheric summit just as soon after the 20th of January as possible to fight that war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But we also have to deal with drug education prevention here at home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And that’s one of the things that I hope I can lead personally as the President of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had great success in my own state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve reached out to young people and their families and been able to help them by beginning drug education and prevention in the early elementary grades.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: So we can fight this war, and we can win this war.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we can do so in a way that marshals our forces, that provides real support for state and local law enforcement officers who have not been getting that support, and do it in a way which will bring down violence in this nation, will help our youngsters to stay away from drugs, will stop this avalanche of drugs that’s pouring into the country, and will make it possible for our kids and our families to grow up in safe and secure and decent neighborhoods.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, a lot of what this campaign is about, it seems to me Bernie, goes to the question of values.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And here I do have, on this particular question, a big difference with my opponent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You see, I do believe that some crimes are so heinous, so brutal, so outrageous, and I’d say particularly those that result in the death of a police officer, for those real brutal crimes, I do believe in the death penalty, and I think it is a deterrent, and I believe we need it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m glad that the Congress moved on this drug bill and have finally called for that related to these narcotics drug kingpins.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so we just have an honest difference of opinion: I support it and he doesn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Bernie.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’d have confidence in him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I made a good selection.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve never seen such a pounding, an unfair pounding, on a young Senator in my entire life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve never seen a presidential campaign where the presidential nominee runs against my vice presidential nominee; never seen one before.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But you know, Lloyd Bentsen jumped on Dan Quayle, when Dan Quayle said, he’s had roughly the same amount of experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He had two terms in the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He had two terms in the Senate, serving his second term.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He founded authored, the job training partnership act.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It says to American working men and women that are thrown out of work for no fault of their own that they’re going to have jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re moving into a new competitive age, and we need that kind of thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He, unlike my opponent, is an expert in national defense; helped amend the INF treaty so we got a good, sound treaty, when these people over here were talking about a freeze.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If we’d listened to them, we would never have had a treaty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I have great confidence in him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s turning around.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, the American people are fair.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They don’t like it when there’s an unfair pounding and kind of hooting about people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They want to judge it on the record itself.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I’m proud of my choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And you know, I don’t think age is the only criterion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I’ll tell you something, I’m proud that people who are 30 years old and 40 years old now have someone in their generation that is going to be vice president of the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I made a good selection.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The American people are seeing it, and I’m proud of it; that’s what I’d say.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he could do the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bernard, this was the first presidential decision that we as nominees were called upon to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why people are so concerned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Because it was an opportunity for us to demonstrate what we were looking for in a running mate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: More than that, it was the first national security decision that we had to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The Vice President talks about national security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Three times since World War II, the Vice President has had to suddenly become the President and commander in chief.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I picked Lloyd Bentsen, because I thought he was the best qualified person for the job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: GOY.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush picked Dan Quayle, and before he did it, he said, watch my choice for vice president, it will tell all And it sure did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It sure did.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, because I’m pledged to that, and yes, some taxes have gone up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the main point is, taxes have been cut, and yet income is up to the Federal Government by 25 percent in the last three years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so what I want to do is keep this expansion going.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to kill it off by a tax increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: More Americans at work today than at any time in the history of the country, and a greater percentage of the work force.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the way you kill expansions is to raise taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t want to do that, and I won’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And what I have proposed is something much better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s going to take discipline of the executive branch; it’s going to take discipline of the congressional branch.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that is what I call a flexible freeze that allows growth about 4 percent or the rate of inflation but does not permit the Congress just to add on spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I hear this talk about a blank check.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The American people are pretty smart: they know who writes out the checks.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And they know who appropriates the money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is the United States Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And by two to one, Congress is blamed for these deficits.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the answer is to discipline both the executive branch and the congressional branch by holding the line on taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I’m pledged to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And those pessimists who say it can’t be done, I’m sorry, I just have a fundamental disagreement with them

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Ann, the Vice President made that pledge.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: He’s broken it three times in the past year already.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: So it isn’t worth the paper it’s printed on.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And what I’m concerned about is that if we continue with the policies that Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush is talking about here this evening, the flexible freeze somebody described it the other day as a kind of economic slurpee he wants to spend billions on virtually every weapons system around.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: He says he’s not going to raise taxes, though he has broken that pledge repeatedly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: He says he wants to give the wealthiest one percent of the people in this country a five-year $40 billion tax break, and we’re going to pay for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And he’s been proposing all kinds of programs for new spending costing billions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Now if we continue with these policies, this trillion and a half dollars worth of new debt that’s already been added on the backs of the American taxpayer is going to increase even more, and if we continue with this for another four years, then I’m worried about the next generation, whether we can ever turn this situation around.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: No, we need a chief executive who is prepared to lead; who won’t blame the Congress; who will lead to bring down that deficit, who will make tough choices on spending

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: will go out and do the job that we expect of him and do it with the Congress of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: No, I’m not sure I can promise that; I don’t think either one of us can really.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: There is no way of anticipating what may happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I will say this: that we will set as our goal a steady, gradual reduction of the deficit, which will require tough choices on spending; it will require a good strong rate of economic growth; it will require a plan that the president works out with the Congress doesn’t blame them, works it out with them, which brings that deficit down; it will require us to go out and collect billions and billions of dollars in taxes owed that aren’t being paid in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And that’s grossly unfair to the average American who is paying his taxes and paying them on time and doesn’t have any alternative: it’s taken out of his paycheck.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush says we are going to put the IRS on every taxpayer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: That’s not what we are going to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m for the taxpayer bill of rights.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I think it’s unconscionable, Ann, that we should be talking or thinking about imposing new taxes on average Americans when there are billions out there, over $100 billion, in taxes owed that aren’t being paid.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Now, I think if we work together on it, and if you have a president that will work with the Congress and the American people, we can bring that deficit down steadily, $20, $25, $30 billion a year, build economic growth, build a good strong future for America, invest in those things which we must invest in economic development, good jobs, good schools for our kids, college opportunity for young people, decent health care and affordable housing, and a clean and safe environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We can do all of those things, and at the same time build a future in which we are standing on a good strong fiscal foundation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Senator Bentsen said, as you recall at the debate with Senator Quayle, that if you give any of us $200 billion worth of hot checks a year, we can create an illusion of prosperity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But sooner or later that credit card mentality isn’t going to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I want to bring to the White House a sense of strength and fiscal responsibility which will build a good strong foundation under which this country, or above which country can move, grow, invest, and build the best America for its people and for our kids and our grandkids.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Governor has to balance the budget in his state he is required to by law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He has raised taxes several times.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I wish he would join me, as a matter of fact, in appealing to the American people for the balanced budget amendment for the federal government and for the line-item veto.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to have that line-item veto for the president, because I think that would be extraordinarily helpful.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I won’t do one other thing that he’s had to do: took $29 million out of his state pension fund that’s equivalent at the federal level of taking out of the Social Security trust fund.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not going to do that; I won’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I’m still a little unclear as to whether he’s for or against the tax increase.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I have been for the taxpayer bill of rights all along.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And this idea of unleashing a whole bunch-an army, a conventional force army, of IRS agents into everybody’s kitchen I mean, he’s against most defense matters, and now he wants to get an army of JRS auditors going out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m against that; I oppose that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Just a minute.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I don’t know if the vice president agrees with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Margaret, may I go back and just say to the vice president that I didn’t raid the pension fund of Massachusetts you are dead wrong, George, we didn’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, I’m the first governor in the history of my state to fund that pension system, and I’m very proud of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I have been in politics for twenty-five years, Margaret; I’ve won a lot of elections, I’ve lost a few, as you know, and learned from those losses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I won the Democratic nomination in fifty-one separate contests.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think I’m a reasonably likable guy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m serious though I think I’m a little more lovable these days than I used to be back in my youth when I began in my state legislature.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I’m also a serious guy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think the presidency of the United States is a very serious office, and I think we have to address these issues in a very serious way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: So I hope and expect that I will be liked by the people of this country as president of the United States; I certainly hope I will be liked by them on the 8th of November.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I also think it’s important to be somebody who is willing to make those tough choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Now, we have just heard two or three times from the vice president: he’s not going to raise taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I repeat, within days after you made that pledge, you broke it; you said, well, maybe as a last resort we’ll do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And you supported legislation this year that’s involved tax increases not once, but twice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: So that pledge isn’t realistic, and I think the vice president knows it; I think the people of this country know it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The fact of the matter is that the next president of the United States is going to have to go to the White House seriously, he is going to have to work with the Congress seriously he can’t turn to the Congress and blame them for the fact that we don’t have a balanced budget and that we have billions and billions of dollars in red ink.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I am going to be a president who is serious, I hope and expect will be liked by the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But more than that, to do the kind of job that I’m elected to do, will do it with as much good humor as I can, but at the same time will do it in a way which will achieve the goals we want for ourselves and our people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I think we know what they are: a good strong future, a future in which there is opportunity for all of our citizens.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think it’s a question of whether people like you or not to make you an effective leader.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s whether you share the broad dreams of the American people, whether you have confidence in the people’s ability to get things done or whether you think it all should be turned over, as many of the liberals do, to Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You see, I think it’s a question of values, not likability or loveability, it’s a question in foreign affairs in experience, knowing world leaders, knowing how to build on a superb record of this administration in arms control, because you’d know exactly how to begin.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You have to learn from experience that making unilateral cuts in defense system is not the way that you enhance peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’ve got to understand that it is only the United States that can stand for freedom and democracy around the world and we can’t turn it over to the United Nations or other multilateral organizations.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is, though, trying to understand the heartbeat of the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I know these campaigns get knocked a lot, but I think I’d be a better President now for having had to travel to these communities and understand the family values and the importance of neighborhood.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Please.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What was he referring to?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think my dad would be pretty proud of me, because I think we’ve come a long long way and I think, you know three months ago, I remember some of the great publications in this country had written me off.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And what I’ve had to do is define, not just my position, but to define his and I hope I’ve done it fairly.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the reason I’ve had to do that is that he ran on the left in the Democratic primary, ran firmly and ran with conviction and ran on his record.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then at that Democratic convention, they made a determination and they said there, ideology doesn’t matter, just competence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And in the process the negatives began.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It wasn’t me that was there at that convention.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank God I was up in the with Jimmy Baker camping out and I didn’t have to hear all the personal attacks on me out of that Democratic convention.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m not the one that compared the President of the United States rotting from like a dead fish from the head down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I have defined the issues and I am not going to let Governor Dukakis go through this election without explaining some of these very liberal position he’s the one a liberal, traditional liberal a progressive liberal Democrat.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s the one that brought up, to garner primary votes, the whole question of the ACLU.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I have enormous difference with the ACLU on their politic agenda.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Not on their defending some minority opinion on the right or the left.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I support that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But what I don’t like is this left wing political agenda and therefore I have to help define that and if he’s unwilling to do it, if he says ideology doesn’t matter, I don’t agree with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, Margaret, we’ve heard it again tonight and I’m not surprised, the labels.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I guess the Vice President two or three times, said I was coming from the left.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: In 1980, President Reagan called you a liberal for voting for Federal gun control.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And this is something Republicans have used for a long time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: They tried it with Franklin Roosevelt and Harry Truman and John Kennedy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s not labels.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s our vision of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we have two fundamentally different visions of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The Vice President is complacent, thinks we ought to stick with the status quo, doesn’t think we ought to move ahead, thinking things are okay as they are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think this is a great country, because we’ve always wanted to do better, to make our country better, to make our lives better.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve always been a nation which was ambitious for America and we move forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the kind of America I want.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: That’s the kind of leadership I want to provide.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t think these labels mean a thing and I would hope that tonight in the course of the rest of this campaign, we can have good solid disagreements on issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: There’s nothing the matter with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But let’s stop labeling each other and lets’ get to the heart of the matter which is the future of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If I knew of three new weapons systems that I thought were purely waste and weren’t protected by the Congress, they wouldn’t be in the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They would not be in the budget, but you want one now?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ll give you one, that HMET, that heavy truck, that’s cost what is it $850 million and the Pentagon didn’t request it and, yet, a member of Congress, a very powerful one, put it in the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we can save money through this whole very sophisticated concept, Andrea, that I know you do understand of competitive strategies.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is new and it is very very different than what’s happened, but it’s not quite ready to be totally implemented.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But it’s very important.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we can say, through the Packard Commission Report and I’m very proud that David Packard, the originator of that report, is strongly supporting me.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So, it’s not a question of saying our budget is full of a lot of waste.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t believe that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do think this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re in the serious stages of negotiation with the Soviet Union on the strategic arms control talks.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’re protecting a couple of options in terms of modernizing our strategic forces.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My Secretary of Defense is going to have to make a very difficult decision in which system to go forward with.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we are protecting both of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We are moving forward with negotiations and, you see, I just think it would be dumb negotiating policy with the Soviets to cut out one or the other of the two options right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Soviets are modernizing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They continue to modernize and we can’t simply we’ve got enough nuclear weapons, let’s freeze.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have to have modernization, especially if we achieve the 50 percent reduction in strategic weapons that our President is taking the leadership to attain.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And, so, that’s the way I’d reply to it and I believe we can have the strongest and best defense possible if we modernize, if we go forward with competitive strategies and if we do follow through on the Packard Commission report.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, Andrea, we’ve just had another example of why the Vice President’s mathematics just don’t add up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think you know because you’ve covered these issues, that there’s no way that we can build all of the weapons the Vice President says he wants to build within the defense budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Everybody knows that including the people at the Pentagon.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Now, my defense secretary is going to have a lot to do with those decisions, but it’s going to be the President who’s going to have to ultimately decide before that budget goes to the Congress what weapons systems are going to go and what are going to stay.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We are not going to spend the billions and trillions that Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush wants to spend on Star Wars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’re not going to spend billions on MX’s on railroad cars, which is a weapons system we don’t need, can’t afford and won’t help our defense posture at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’re not going to spend hundreds of millions on a space plane from Washington to Tokyo.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Those are decisions that the chief executive has to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Yes, we’re going to have a strong and credible and effective nuclear deterrent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to go forward with the Stealth and the D-5 and the advance cruise missile and good conventional forces.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But the next President of the United States will have to make some tough and difficult decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m prepared to make them, the Vice President is not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, Andrea, today we have 13,000 strategic nuclear warheads, on land, on air and in the sea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: That’s an incredibly powerful nuclear deterrent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I don’t rule out modernization, and there are discussions going on now in the Congress, I know with the Pentagon, about a less expensive modernized land-based leg of the triad.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But there are limits to what we can spend.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: There are limits to this nation’s ability to finance these weapons systems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And one of the things that the Vice President either ignores or won’t address is the fact that you can’t divorce our military security from our economic security.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: How can we build a strong America militarily that’s teeter-tottering on a mountain of debt?

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And if we go forward with the kinds of policies that the Vice President is suggesting tonight and has in the past, that debt is going to grow bigger and bigger and bigger.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: So military security and economic security go hand in hand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we will have a strong and effective and credible nuclear deterrent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have conventional forces that are well maintained, well equipped, well trained, well supported.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we have serious problems with our conventional forces at the present time, and they’ll get worse unless we have a president who is willing to make some of these decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we also have important domestic priorities, in education and housing and health care, in economic development, in job training, in the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And all of these things are going to have to be addressed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I say again to all of you out there who have to deal with your household budgets and know how difficult it is that the next President has to do the same.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I want the men and women of our Armed Forces to have the support they need to defend us; the support they need when they risk our lives to keep us free and to keep this country free.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But we cannot continue to live on a credit card.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We cannot continue to tell the American people that we’re going to build all of these systems, and at the same time, invest in important things here at home, and be serious about building a strong and good America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the kind of America I want to build.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the foremost

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Can we start the clock over?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I held off for the applause.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the foremost responsibility of a president really gets down to the national security of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Governor talks about limits, what we can’t do, opposes these two modernization systems, talks now about well, we’ll develop some new kind of a missile.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It takes eight years, ten years, to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He talked about a nuclear freeze back at the time when I was in Europe trying to convince European public opinion that we ought to go forward with the deployment of the INF weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And thank God, the freeze people were not heard.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They were wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the result is, we deployed, and the Soviets kept deploying, and then we negotiated from strength.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And now we have the first arms control agreement in the nuclear age to ban weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You just don’t make unilateral cuts in the naive hope that the Soviets are going to behave themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: World peace is important, and we have enhanced the peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m proud to have been a part of an administration that has done exactly that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Peace through strength works.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think when I think of heroes, I think back, not presently, Ann.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But there are many people who I admire in this country today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Some of them are in public life in the Senate, the Congress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Some of my fellow governors who are real heroes to me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think of those young athletes who represented us at the Olympics were tremendously impressive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We were proud of them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We felt strongly about them, and they did so well by us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I can think of doctors and scientists, Jonas Salk who for example discovered a vaccine which cured one of the most dread diseases we ever had.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And he’s a hero.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think of classroom teachers, classroom teachers that I have had, classroom teachers that youngsters have today who are real heroes to our young people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Because they inspire them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: They teach them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But more than that, they are role models.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Members of the clergy who have done the same.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Drug counselors out there in the street who are providing help to youngsters who come up to me and others who ask for help and want help, are doing the hard work, the heroic work, which it takes to provide that kind of leadership, that kind of counseling, that kind of support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think of people in the law enforcement community who are taking their lives in their hands everyday, when they go up to one of those doors and kick it down and try to stop this flow of drugs into our communities and into our kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: So there are many, many heroes in this country today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: These are people that give of themselves everyday and every week and every month.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: In many cases they are people in the community who are examples, and are role models.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I would hope that one of the things I could do as president is to recognize them, to give them the kind of recognition that they need and deserve so that more and more young people can themselves become the heroes of tomorrow, can go into public service, can go into teaching, can go into drug counseling, can go into law enforcement, and be heroes themselves to generations yet to come.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think of a teacher right here, largely Hispanic school, Jaime Escalante, teaching calculus to young kids, 80 percent of them going on to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think of a young man now in this country named Villadaris, who was released from a Cuban jail.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Came out and told the truth in this brilliant book, Against All Hope, about what is actually happening in Cuba.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think of those people that took us back into space again, Rick Houk and that crew, as people that are worthy of this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I agree with the Governor on athletics.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And there’s nothing corny about having sports heroes, young people that are clean and honorable and out there setting the pace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think of Dr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Fauci.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Probably never heard of him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You did, Ann heard of him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s a very fine research, top doctor, at the National Institute of Health, working hard doing something about research on this disease of AIDS.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But look, I also think we ought to give a little credit to the President of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He is the one who has gotten us that first arms control agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the cynics abounded.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he is leaving office with a popularity at an all-time high, because American people

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: say, he is our hero.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You’re stealing my close.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I had something very nice to say in there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No, let me tell you something about that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And Barbara and I were sitting there before that Democratic convention.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we saw the Governor and his son on television the night before and his family, and his mother who was there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’m saying to Barbara, you know, we’ve always kept family as a bit of an oasis for us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You all know me, and we’ve held it back a little.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we used that as a role model, the way he took understandable pride in his heritage, what his family means to him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got a strong family.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we watched that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we said, hey, we’ve got to unleash the Bush kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so you saw ten grandchildren there jumping all over their grandfather at the convention.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You see our five kids, all over this country, and their spouses.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I would say that the concept of the Dukakis family has my great respect.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I would say, I don’t know whether that’s kind or not, it’s just an objective statement.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the man anybody that gets into this political arena and has to face you guys everyday deserves a word of praise.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because it’s gotten a little ugly out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s gotten a little nasty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not much fun sometimes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I would cite again Dan Quayle.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been in politics a long time, and I don’t remember that kind of piling on, that kind of ugly rumor that never was true, printed.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, come on.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So some of it is unfair.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But he’s in the arena.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Teddy Roosevelt used to talk about the arena, you know, daring to fail greatly or succeed, no matter.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He’s in there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So I salute these things.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I salute those who participate in the political process.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Sam Raybum had a great expression on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He said here were all these intellectuals out there griping and complaining and saying it was negative coverage.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Rayburn says, yeah, and that guy never ran for sheriff either.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Michael Dukakis has run for sheriff, and so has George Bush.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t hear the word “liberal” or “left” one time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I thank you for that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s not bad.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s true.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And doesn’t that prove the point, George, which is that values like family and education and community, decent homes for young people that family on Long Island I visited on Monday where Lou and Betty Tolamo bought a house for some $19,000 back in 1962, have had seven children, they’re all making good livings.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: They can’t live in the community which they grew up in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Those are basic American values.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I believe in them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think you believe in them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: They’re not left or right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: They’re decent American values.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I guess the one thing that concerns me about this, Ann, is this attempt to label things which all of us believe in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We may have different approaches.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We may think that you deal with them in different ways.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But they’re basically American, I believe in them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: George Bush believes in them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think the vast majority of Americans believe in them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I hope

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: the tone we’ve just heard might just be the tone we have for the rest of the campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think the American people would appreciate that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because you left out one other exception, the health of the mother.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me answer your question and I hope it doesn’t get too personal or maudlin.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Barb and I lost a child, you know that we lost a daughter, Robin.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I was over running records in west Texas, and I got a call from her, come home; went to the doctor; the doctor said, beautiful child, your child has a few weeks to live.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I said, what can we do about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He said, no, she has leukemia, acute leukemia, a few weeks to live.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We took the child to New York.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thanks to the miraculous sacrifice of doctors and nurses, the child stayed alive for six months and then died.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: If that child were here today, and I was told the same thing, my granddaughter, Noel for example that child could stay alive for ten or fifteen years, or maybe for the rest of her life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I don’t think that you make an exception based on medical knowledge at the time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think human life is very, very precious.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And, look, this hasn’t been an easy decision for me to meet.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know others disagree with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But when I was in that little church across the river from Washington and saw our grandchild christened in our faith, I was very pleased indeed that the mother had not aborted that child, and put the child up for adoption.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I just feel this is where I’m coming from.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it is personal.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t assail him on that issue, or others on that issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But that’s the way I, George Bush, feel about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Margaret, Kitty and I had very much the same kind of experience that the Bushes had: we lost a baby, lived about twenty minutes after it was born.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But isn’t the real question that we have to answer not how many exceptions we make, because the vice president himself is prepared to make exceptions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s who makes the decision, who makes this very difficult, very wrenching decision?

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I think it has to be the woman, in the exercise of her own conscience and religious beliefs, that makes that decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Who are we to say, well, under certain circumstances, it’s all right, but under other circumstances it isn’t?

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: That’s a decision that only a woman can make, after consulting her conscience and consulting her religious principles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I would hope that we would give to women in this country the right to make that decision, and to make it in the exercise of their conscience and religious beliefs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And, incidentally, may I say that that’s the decision of the Congress, and the president has concurred.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think I was on the advisory committee, Margaret.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: No, I don’t happen to share that goal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s an example of how oftentimes we may be associated with organizations all of whose particular positions we don’t support, even though we support in general the hope that over time, particularly if we can get those reductions in strategic weapons, if we can get a comprehensive test ban treaty, if we can negotiate with the Soviet Union and bring down the level of conventional forces in Europe with deeper cuts in the Soviet side, yes, at some point it may be possible to reduce defense outlays and use those for important things here at home, like jobs and job training and college opportunity and health and housing and the environment and the things that all of us care about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I do think this, that the next president, even within a relatively stable budget and that’s what we are going to have for the foreseeable future will have to make those tough choices that I was talking about and that Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush doesn’t seem to want to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And that really is going to be a challenge for the next president of the United States; I don’t think there’s any question about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I also see a tremendous opportunity now to negotiate with the Soviet Union to build on the progress that we’ve made with the INF Treaty, which I strongly supported and most Democrats did to get those reductions in strategic weapons, to get a test ban treaty, and to really make progress on the reduction of conventional forces in Europe.

transcript_turns.text: Not working with government alone, but all of us working together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Lloyd Bentsen and I are optimists, and so are the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we ask you for our hand for your hands and your hearts, and your votes on the 8th of November so we can move forward in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Kitty and I are very grateful to all of you for the warmth and the hospitality that you’ve given to us in your homes and communities all across this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We love you, and we’re grateful to you for everything that you’ve given to us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we hope that we’ll be serving you in the White House in January of 1989.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, and God bless you.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Sometimes it does seem that a campaign generates more heat than light.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So let me repeat, I do have respect for my opponent, for his family, for the justifiable pride he takes in his heritage.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we have enormous differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to hold the line on taxes, and keep this the longest expansion in modern history going until everybody in America benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to invest in our children.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because I mean it when I say I want a kinder and gentler nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And by that I want to have child care where the families, the parents, have control.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to keep our neighborhoods much, much better in terms of anti-crime, and that’s why I would appoint judges that have a little more sympathy for the victims of crime and a little less for the criminals.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I do feel if some police officer is gunned down that the death penalty is required.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to help those with disabilities fit into the mainstream.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There is much to be done.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This election is about big things.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And perhaps the biggest is world peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I ask you to consider the experience I have had in working with a President who has revolutionized the situation around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: America stands tall again, and as a result, we are credible.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we have now achieved an historic arms control agreement.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to build on that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’d love to be able to say to my grandchildren, four years after my first term, I’d like to say, your grandfather, working with the leaders of the Soviet Union, working with the leaders of Europe, was able to ban chemical and biological weapons from the face of the earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Lincoln called this country the last best hope of man on earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he was right then, and we still are the last best hope of man on earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I ask for your support on November 8th.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I will be a good president.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Working together, we can do wonderful things for the United States and the Free World.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very, very much.
